segmenti.tekst: نحن نقص عليك أحسن القصص بما أوحينا إليك هذا القرآن وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين. الحمد لله رب العالمين، والصلاة والسلام على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وصحبه أجمعين. We continue with the tafsir (exegesis) of Surah Yusuf. After the stories spread around the city that the mayor's wife had tried to seduce Yusuf into zina (fornication),

and after the women began to pass this around, the wives of the wealthy, the rich, this wife of the prime minister decided to invite them to a banquet. So she prepared a banquet for them and a nice place where they could recline and enjoy themselves, and she brought them utensils for the food, utensils that of course included a knife, and when Yusuf came out before them, they cut themselves, because they were overwhelmed by his beauty.
And they said: "This is not a man, this is not a human being, this is an angel." When Yusuf saw that things had gone too far, he turned to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.
And a believer, dear brothers, whenever he is in a difficult situation, to whom does he turn? To Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. What does Yusuf say?
[Arabic recitation]
Because the mayor's wife had said: "If," she says, "he does not do what I ask of him,
we will imprison him." So Yusuf says: "Qala Rabbis-sijnu ahabbu ilayya" – he says: "My Lord, prison is dearer to me than that to which they are inviting me." So Yusuf was choosing between two evils:
either prison or zina. And there is a Shari'ah principle: when a person faces two evils and cannot avoid either of them, he must choose, and he always chooses the lesser evil.

It is interesting that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, uses the plural in this ayah. He says: "My Lord, prison is dearer to me than that to which they invite me." Why "they," when only the wife of this prime minister had invited him to fornication? The mufassirun (Qur'an commentators) say: when the other women also saw at that evening, at that banquet, how beautiful Yusuf was, they too began to invite him to fornication, to zina.

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, further says: "And," he says, "O my Allah, if You do not turn their schemes away from me – asbu ilayhinna" – he says: "I fear, I fear that I will do what they invite me to, that I will succumb to their schemes, and be among the ignorant." For only an ignorant person gives preference to the passing world over eternal life.

That is a trait of the ignorant. An Arab poet says: "La khayra fi ladhdhatin min ba'diha saqar." He says: there is no good, no good in a pleasure, in an enjoyment followed by Saqar, by Jahannam (Hellfire).
So it is out of ignorance, out of foolishness, that a person, for one small, brief, worldly pleasure, destroys, destroys his Hereafter.

What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say next? "Fastajaba lahu Rabbuhu" – so Allah, He says, immediately answered his supplication – "fa sarafa 'anhu kaydahunn" – and, He says, turned away from him the schemes of these women. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in the Qur'an: "Wa idha sa'alaka 'ibadi 'anni fa inni qarib" – and when My servants ask you about Me, O Muhammad – "inni qarib" – He says: I am near, I am near –
"ujibu da'watad-da'i idha da'an" – I respond to the request of the one who asks of Me, who calls upon Me. And that is why, whenever a person is in a difficult situation, what does he do?

He should pray to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, [unclear]. See how Allah immediately answered the supplication of Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam. Why? Because Yusuf was His sincere servant. "Truly, He is the One who hears," who hears everything, hears the supplications of His servants; al-'Alim – the One who knows, who knows everything, who knows the state that every human being is in. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, then tells us what happens to Yusuf.

After Yusuf said that he would rather go to prison than commit what they were inviting him to, and after… after the proofs of his innocence had been laid before this prime minister of Egypt and his associates, they nevertheless decided to imprison him.

Even though Yusuf was known for his honesty, and even though that witness had testified that she was guilty, and despite everything that had happened to him, they nevertheless decided to imprison him.

And this, as the mufassirun say, was the fifth great trial for Yusuf. The first was being thrown into the well. The second was being sold as a slave. They sold him as a slave – selling a free man as a slave is a great sin.

The third was the seduction attempt by the wife of this prime minister. The fourth was the seduction attempt by those women who came to see who this Yusuf was. And the fifth is this, this prison. And there is nothing strange about that; the Prophet Muhammad says: the people most severely tested are the prophets.

And our Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), is the man who was tested the most. There is no man who was tested more than him. His parents passed away while he was small; that is, his father passed away before he was born.

His mother passed away when he was six years old. All his children passed away before his death, before his passing, except Fatimah. His own people [unclear], and so on, and so forth. So the prophets are the people who are tested the most. The most tested are the prophets, he says, the prophets… He also says: a person will be tested, a person will be tested in proportion

to the strength of his iman, to how strong his faith is. So if a person's iman is strong, Allah will test him more and more. The person becomes hardened. Just like iron being forged: the more the blacksmith strikes it, the stronger it becomes. So too the mu'min: whenever some misfortune strikes him, after it he is always, always stronger. And Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, announces this to us in the Qur'an, saying: "We will," He says, "test you with fear, hunger, and loss of lives and fruits."
What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say? "Wa bashshiris-sabirin" – and, He says, give glad tidings to those, He says, who are patient. Those who, when some misfortune strikes them, say what?

"Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un" – truly we belong to Allah and to Allah we return. This faith, dear brothers, cannot be carried without sacrifice. It cannot be done without sacrifice. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Ahasiban-nasu…, ahasiban-nasu…"
He says: does a person think, do people think that if they say "we believe" they will be left alone? It cannot be. As soon as you say "I believe," know that there will be trials.

All of you have had similar trials, that is, we all have similar trials. When a person first starts to pray, to come to the mosque – isn't that so? – what is the first thing that starts? The parents say: "What's with that beard?

Why do you go? Why do you keep bobbing up and down five times a day?" Then a relative comes – you won't shake hands with your female relative, because it is haram: "Why won't you shake hands? What do you mean you won't?" And attacks from this side and from that side, and so on, and so forth, from all kinds of people. So this faith is just like a burning ember, like a burning ember, and only the one who is strong enough, strong enough will hold on to it, as Yusuf, alayhis-salatu was-salam, was. As-salamu alaykum.
